b1-n-personal: You praise a hotel to your friend: the receptionists, cleaners and cooks who work there are all friendly. Which noun means all these workers together?
A company has 200 employees. The boss says the group of people who work there will grow next year. Which word means 'staff'?
A restaurant sign says, 'Our team of waiters and cooks is happy to help.' You want the noun for the whole group of workers.
b1-v-einfallen: You stand in a shop and have no idea what to buy for your mother. Suddenly a good idea pops into your head.
You try to recall the name of your old teacher. After a minute it suddenly comes back to you. What do you do when a thought comes to your mind?
In a meeting nobody knows the answer, then a clever solution suddenly occurs to you. Which verb means 'to occur to someone'?
b1-n-strafe: You park in a no-parking zone and find a paper under your windshield saying you must pay 30 euros.
A boy breaks a window while playing football. His parents take away his phone for a week so he learns his lesson.
The judge says the man must pay 500 euros for driving too fast. Which noun means 'punishment'?
b1-adj-reif: You squeeze a banana at the market. It is soft, yellow and sweet, no longer green, and ready to eat.
Your 17-year-old cousin handles money and problems like a sensible adult, much more grown-up than most boys his age.
The tomatoes in the garden have turned red and can be picked now. Which adjective describes the fruit?
b1-n-korridor: In a hospital you walk along a long, narrow passage with doors to many rooms on both sides.
At school the students wait in the long passage outside the classroom before the lesson starts.
Your hotel room is at the end of a long passage with identical doors in a row. Which noun means 'corridor'?
b1-n-freude: You open the door and see your best friend from abroad. Your heart fills with a big, happy feeling.
A girl gets a puppy for her birthday and jumps up and down with happiness.
You write on a card to a friend: 'Your visit gave us so much of this.' Which noun means 'joy'?
b1-v-auswaehlen: A bakery has twenty kinds of cake. You look at all of them and then pick one.
On a website you look at a seat map for your flight and pick the seat you like best.
Your boss shows you three photos and asks you to pick the best one for the poster. Which verb means 'to select'?
b1-n-theorie: At driving school you first learn rules and road signs from a book, before you sit in a car. This part is not practice.
A scientist has an explanation for why the dinosaurs disappeared, but nobody has proved it yet.
Your friend says: 'It sounds easy in this, but in practice it is hard.' Which noun is the opposite of 'practice'?
b1-adv-einerseits: You talk about moving to a big city. You name the first good point and know you will add the opposite point later. Which word means 'on the one hand'?
You think about buying a car: it is comfortable, but expensive. Which word starts your first point, before the second side?
You weigh two sides of a problem. Which word introduces the first side, 'on the one hand'?
b1-adj-maximal: A sign in the lift says no more than 8 people may ride at once. That is the highest allowed number.
You want the greatest possible effect, so you turn the volume knob to the very top.
Your teacher says you may take at most ten minutes for each question. Which word means 'maximum'?
b1-n-schaden: A tree fell on your neighbor's car in the storm, and the roof is dented. You phone the insurance about it.
You drop your phone and the screen cracks. How big is the harm done?
The doctor warns that smoking does a lot of harm to your lungs. Which noun means 'damage'?
b1-v-nachschlagen: You do not know a word in your book, so you open your dictionary and search for it.
In the library you open a big encyclopedia to find facts about Berlin.
You are not sure how a word is spelled, so you check it in an online dictionary. What do you do?
b1-n-fernbedienung: You sit on the sofa and want to change the TV channel without getting up. You search between the cushions for the small device with buttons.
The TV will not switch on. Your dad says the batteries in the small device are empty.
Which noun means the 'remote control' that lets you change the TV from far away?
b1-n-medien: Newspapers, television, radio and the internet bring news to people. What are they called as a group?
A teacher shows students how to think carefully about what they read in newspapers and see on TV.
Reporters from many newspapers and TV channels wait outside the stadium for the coach. Which plural noun means 'media'?
b1-v-wiegen: At the post office the clerk puts your parcel on a scale to see how heavy it is.
You step on the bathroom scale to find out how many kilos you are.
At the vegetable stand the seller puts apples on the scale. Which verb means 'to weigh'?
b1-n-zwiebel: You chop a round vegetable with many layers for the soup, and tears run down your face.
In autumn you plant small round things from the garden shop in the soil, and tulips grow from them in spring.
Your burger comes with tomato, cheese and rings of a sharp-smelling vegetable. Which noun is that vegetable?
b1-adj-sozial: Your neighbor helps old people with their shopping for free. She cares about others and the community.
A job at the city office is about helping poor families and people in difficult situations.
Which adjective describes anything that is about people living together in society?
b1-n-schreiben: A formal paper arrives from the city office in an envelope. It explains a new rule.
The school sends you an official written message about the parents' evening.
In an exam you must write a text with a pen. Along with reading, listening and speaking it is the fourth skill. Which noun means 'writing'?
b1-n-grill: On a sunny Sunday in the garden you put sausages and meat on a metal rack over hot coals.
Friends are coming for a party, so you buy charcoal for the device you cook meat on outdoors.
You say: 'Let's have a barbecue!' Which noun is the equipment you use for it?
b1-v-sorgen: Your sister goes on holiday and asks you to look after her cat. You promise to feed it every day.
Before the party the boss says: 'Please make sure there are enough drinks.' You say you will arrange it.
Parents work hard to provide food, clothes and a home for their children. Which verb means 'to take care'?
b1-n-teppich: In the living room the floor is covered with a soft woven cover. Your cat sleeps on it, and you vacuum it every week.
In a shop in Turkey you admire a large hand-woven cover with colorful patterns for the floor.
You spill red wine on the floor covering in your hotel room, and the manager says it must be cleaned.
b1-n-minderheit: In the vote only 3 of 10 people said yes, so their group was smaller than the other group.
In a town a small group of people speak a different language from most of the people.
In your class 25 students are girls and 5 are boys. The boys are the smaller part. Which noun means 'minority'?
b1-adj-weiterer: You have eaten one portion but are still hungry, so you ask the waiter for one more portion. Which adjective goes before the noun?
You already have one key, but the landlord gives you an extra one. Which adjective means 'additional'?
At the doctor you are asked if you have any other questions. Which adjective means 'further' or 'other'?
b1-v-warnen: You see the floor is wet in the supermarket and tell a customer to be careful before she slips.
The radio tells people that a big storm is coming tonight, so they should stay at home.
Your friend wants to buy a car from a dishonest seller. You tell him not to, because you know the seller cheats.
b1-n-sonder: A shop sign says the cheap price is only for this week, not normal. Which first part of a German compound noun means 'special' (as in a 'special offer')?
Football fans take an extra train that runs only on match day. Which word part means 'special' at the start of its name?
A bakery bakes a cake that is not on the usual menu, only for Christmas. Which prefix means 'special'?
b1-adv-durcheinander: You open your child's room: toys, clothes and books lie everywhere, all mixed up.
You drop your papers and they land on the floor in no order at all.
After the shocking news your thoughts are in a mess and you cannot think clearly. Which adverb describes this?
b1-n-aktivitaet: At a holiday camp the leader gives a program: swimming, hiking and games. Each item is something you can do in your free time.
A hotel offers yoga, tennis and a cooking class. Each item on the list is one of these.
The doctor says physical movement like daily walks is good for your heart. Which noun means 'activity'?
b1-n-vollzeit: You work eight hours a day, five days a week, at the office, while your friend only works four hours a day.
A job ad says: 'We need a nurse for 40 hours per week, not part of the day.'
Your sister asks her boss to change from half days to all the working hours of a normal week. Which noun means 'full-time'?
b1-v-hochladen: You took photos on holiday and now send them from your computer to a website so others can see them.
Your teacher asks you to send your homework file to the school portal on the internet.
You made a video and put it on the internet platform so everyone can watch it. Which verb means 'to upload'?
b1-adj-ungewoehnlich: It snows in your city in July. Nobody has ever seen this before.
Your friend wears green hair and a very strange hat. People stare because it is not what people normally do.
A restaurant serves ice cream with fish. It is strange and not common at all.
b1-n-geschlecht: On a form you tick 'male' or 'female'. The box is labeled with this word.
At the doctor the ultrasound shows whether the baby is a boy or a girl. Which noun means 'sex' in this sense?
In your German class the teacher says every noun is masculine, feminine or neuter. Which noun names this property?
b1-n-tal: You hike up a mountain. From the top you look down at the low land between two hills, with a river and a village.
The village lies at the bottom between high mountains, and a river flows through it.
Which noun means the low land between two mountains?
b1-v-stossen: In a crowded bus you hit your head on the low door frame.
You walk in the dark and your foot hits the leg of the table. Which verb means 'to bump'?
During your research you come across a surprising old photo you did not expect to find.
b1-n-protest: Hundreds of students walk through the street with signs, shouting that they do not accept the higher bus prices.
You think a new rule is unfair, so you loudly say 'No!' in the meeting.
Neighbors collect names on a paper to show they are against a new road. Which noun means 'protest'?
b1-n-ente: At the park pond a bird with a flat beak swims and says 'quack'. Children throw bread to it.
At a Chinese restaurant you order a crispy roast bird with orange sauce, but it is not chicken.
A yellow rubber toy floats in the baby's bath. It is shaped like a bird that says 'quack'.
b1-adj-verstaendlich: Your teacher explains grammar so simply that everyone in the class gets it.
The instructions for the machine are written in clear, easy words, so anyone can follow them.
Your friend lost his job and cries. You say you can easily see why he feels this way. Which adjective means 'understandable'?
b1-v-leidtun: You accidentally step on a stranger's foot on the bus and want to say how bad you feel about it.
Your friend's grandfather died. You tell him you feel sad for him.
You arrive an hour late to a meeting and tell your boss you regret it. Which verb means 'to feel sorry'?
b1-n-vorwurf: Your mother says angrily: 'You never help in the house!' She is blaming you for something.
A customer says the shop cheated him, and the owner denies it. This claim that someone did wrong is called what?
Your friend did not call for weeks. You tell him how disappointed you were, and it sounds like blame.
b1-n-schein: At the cash desk you pay with a paper note of 20 euros, not with coins.
You show your swimming teacher the paper that proves you passed the test.
In a dark room you see only the weak glow of a candle. Which noun means this light?
b1-n-maus: A small grey animal with a long tail runs across the kitchen floor, and the cat chases it.
Your laptop pad does not work, so you plug in a small device with two buttons and click with your hand.
In the cartoon a famous character with round ears and a squeaky voice is this animal.
b1-v-genehmigen: You asked your boss for two weeks of holiday. She signs the paper and says yes, it is allowed.
The city office checks your plan for a new garage and officially says you may build it.
Your bank accepts your request for a loan. Which verb means 'to approve'?
b1-adv-werktags: A parking sign says the fee applies on every normal working day, but not on Sundays.
Your gym offers a cheaper ticket that is only valid on working days.
A shop is open Monday to Saturday. Which adverb means 'on working days'?
b1-n-hoffnung: Your friend is very sick. You believe she will get well soon, and you wish for it.
You wait for your exam results and wish with all your heart that you passed.
After months without work you got an interview. It gives you a good feeling that things may get better.
b1-adj-optimistisch: It rains hard on your wedding day, but you smile and say it will surely be fine later.
Your friend failed the exam but says the next time will be better. He always sees the bright side.
Which adjective describes a person who expects good things to happen?
b1-n-kanne: At breakfast you pour hot coffee from a container with a handle and a spout into the cups.
In the garden you fill a metal container with water to water the flowers.
In a restaurant you ask for a big container of water for the table, and the waiter brings one made of glass with a handle.
b1-v-drehen: You hold a key in the door lock and move it in a circle to open the door.
To make the radio louder you move the knob around to the right.
The big wheel at the fair slowly goes round and round. Which verb means 'to rotate'?
b1-n-betreuer: At the summer camp a young man looks after the children, plays with them and keeps them safe.
At a care home a man helps old people with eating and walking.
During your internship at a company, a man guides you and checks your work. What do you call him?
b1-n-frieden: Two neighbors who argued for years finally shake hands. There is no more quarrel, and everything is calm.
Children draw a white dove at school and write a wish for a world without war.
Two countries sign an agreement to end a long conflict. Which noun means 'peace'?
b1-adj-gesamt: You add the prices of all the items in your basket and see the final sum at the end.
The teacher says the entire class must stay after school, not only two students.
A company has 5000 workers in all its countries together. Which adjective means 'total' or 'whole'?
b1-n-zweifel: A salesman says the car has never had an accident, but you are not sure you can believe him.
You wonder if you chose the right job, and a small voice says maybe not.
The police have no uncertainty about who the thief is. Which noun means 'doubt'?
b1-v-springen: Children at the swimming pool run to the edge and push off with both feet into the water.
A frog moves quickly from one stone to another by pushing off with its legs.
In the gym the coach says: 'Leave the ground with both feet, again and again, to warm up.'
b1-n-kranke: In the hospital ward a man lies in bed with a fever, and the nurse checks on him.
A volunteer visits a man who is too ill to leave his house and brings him food.
The doctor says a man who is ill should rest at home. What do you call the man?
b1-n-entwicklung: A baby first crawls, then walks, then speaks. The doctor checks how the child is progressing.
A company creates new software over many months. This process of making something new is called what?
The news reports how prices have changed over the last ten years.
b1-v-einbrechen: Thieves get into a house at night through a window, and the police are called.
A heavy load of snow makes the old roof of the barn fall in.
A man walks on thin ice on a lake, and it breaks under him. Which verb means 'to cave in'?
b1-n-giraffe: At the zoo an animal with a very long neck eats leaves from the top of a tall tree.
In Africa lives a yellow animal with brown spots, the tallest animal in the world.
A child's drawing shows an animal that is taller than the house, with a neck like a tower.
b1-adj-salzig: The soup tastes too much of salt, and you drink a lot of water afterwards.
At the cinema you prefer crisps and peanuts over sweets, because you like this taste more.
Sea water has a strong taste. Which adjective describes it?
b1-n-lehre: After school sixteen-year-old Anna works three years at a bakery and goes to vocational school to become a baker.
The story ends with a moral: do not lie. What the story teaches you is called what?
After the accident you learned something important for the future: always check the brakes.
b1-adv-bereits: You ask a colleague whether he has finished the report. He says it is done, even earlier than expected.
You arrive at 8 o'clock and your friend is there, since he came before you.
The teacher is surprised that you finished the test so early. Which adverb means 'already'?
b1-v-sich-erkundigen: Before buying a ticket you go to the information desk and ask what time the train leaves.
You phone the hotel to find out whether they have a free room and what the price is.
A friend is in hospital, so you call to ask how he is. Which verb means 'to inquire'?
b1-n-vergleich: In the shop you look at two phones side by side and check price and battery.
The teacher gives you two poems and asks you to say how they are alike and how they are different.
A test magazine puts ten washing machines in a table and rates each one. What is this called?
b1-n-tierpark: On Sunday your family goes to a big park where you can see lions, monkeys and elephants.
On a school trip the children go to see animals from different countries in enclosures.
Which noun means a place where you can visit wild animals?
b1-adj-hungrig: It is 3 pm, you skipped lunch, and your stomach is growling loudly.
After a long hike you would like a big plate of pasta because your belly is empty.
The baby is crying and wants milk. Which adjective describes how the baby feels?
b1-n-kindheit: Your grandfather tells stories about the time when he was small, played in the village and went to primary school.
In an interview someone says that in his early years they had no TV.
Which noun means the time of life before you are a teenager?
b1-v-wenden: The driver realizes the car is going the wrong way and wants to turn it around.
You cook a pancake and flip it in the pan to cook the other side.
You finish a page of the book and move it over to read the next one. Which verb means 'to turn'?
b1-n-rand: Your teacher says to write notes in the white space beside the text on the page.
Be careful with the glass: do not fill it to the very top, up to the rim.
Do not stand so near the end of the cliff. Which noun means 'edge'?
b1-n-turm: At the old church a tall narrow part with bells rises above the roof, and you climb the stairs for the view.
In a medieval castle guards look out from a tall round building.
Paris is famous for a tall iron structure that is higher than all buildings. Which noun means 'tower'?
b1-v-vorschlagen: Your friend does not know what to do on Saturday, and you say: 'Why don't we go to the cinema?'
In a meeting the team leader offers an idea for a new date for the event.
The waiter says you should try the fish soup. He is doing this.
b1-n-ratschlag: You are unsure which job to choose and ask your uncle what you should do. He gives you this.
A friend gives you a useful tip: 'Learn ten words every day.'
Which noun means 'advice' as a single helpful suggestion?
b1-adj-geeignet: You look for shoes for a long mountain hike, and sandals are not right for this.
The job needs a patient person, and you decide the candidate is a good match.
A hotel room for a family with four kids: a single room is not appropriate. Which adjective means 'suitable'?
b1-n-garderobe: At the theatre you hand over your coat and get a numbered tag. Which noun is the room where coats are kept?
In the hallway of the flat there is a place on the wall with hooks to hang jackets.
The actress has a huge collection of dresses and shoes, her whole set of clothes.
b1-n-kuh: On the farm a big black-and-white animal gives milk every morning.
In the Swiss mountains large animals with bells around their necks eat grass on the meadow.
Your child asks which animal says 'moo'.
b1-v-ueberlegen: The salesman wants an answer now, but you say you need time to think about the offer first.
Your friend asks if you will move to Berlin. You say you must weigh it carefully.
Before choosing a university you think for several days about the pros and cons. Which verb means 'to consider'?
b1-n-kopie: At the office you put a paper in the machine and get a second identical sheet.
The office asks for a paper copy of your passport, so you go to the print shop.
A painting in the museum is not the original, but a replica of it.
b1-adv-genauso: Your brother is 180 cm tall and you are 180 cm too. Which adverb means 'just as'?
You compare two phones. This one is exactly as expensive as the other. Which adverb means 'equally'?
A friend says she loves pizza, and you say you feel just the same.
b1-n-uebung: Your teacher gives you ten grammar tasks to do at home so that you can practice.
At the gym the trainer shows a movement for your back that you repeat 15 times.
Pianists play scales every day. This repeated training is called what?
b1-adj-unterschiedlich: Twins look the same, but their characters are not the same at all. One is quiet and one is loud.
The prices in the shops are not the same. One costs 5 euros and another 9.
The weather in April keeps changing, sometimes sunny and sometimes rainy. Which adjective means 'variable' or 'different'?
b1-v-verzeihen: Your friend forgot your birthday and says sorry. You say it is okay and you are not angry anymore.
You said something rude to your sister, and you ask her to let it go.
Someone bumps into you and says sorry, and you say no problem. Which verb means 'to forgive'?
b1-n-jahrtausend: The pyramids are about 4500 years old, which is several periods of one thousand years.
On New Year's Eve in 2000 people celebrated the start of a new period of one thousand years.
One thousand years make up one of these. Which noun means 'millennium'?
b1-n-nagel: To hang a picture you hammer a small thin metal spike into the wall.
At the beauty salon you paint the hard plates at the tips of your fingers red.
In a carpenter's box you find screws and these. Which noun means 'nail'?
b1-v-beobachten: You sit on a bench in the park and quietly look at the birds to see what they do.
A scientist watches how plants grow every day and writes notes.
The teacher says: 'Look closely at the experiment and note what happens.'
b1-n-tram: In the city center you take an electric vehicle on rails along the street. It is not a bus and not an underground train.
In Vienna you buy a ticket for the street rail line that rolls through the city and rings a bell.
A yellow rail car passes your window every ten minutes and stops at the stop in the street.
b1-adj-sinnlos: You studied all night for an exam that was already cancelled, so all your work was for nothing.
Your friend says it makes no sense to wait for the bus because the last one already left.
Digging a hole and filling it again is a task with no purpose at all.
b1-n-herausforderung: Your boss gives you a very difficult project that will test your skills, and you want to try.
Running a marathon on your first try is hard, but you like such tough tasks.
Learning German while working a full-time job is difficult. Which noun means 'challenge'?
b1-n-folge: If you do not wear a seat belt, a bad thing can happen as an effect. What do you call what follows from an action?
Last night you watched the new part of your favorite series on TV.
In math the numbers 2, 4, 6, 8 stand in a fixed order, one after another.
b1-v-hassen: You feel a very strong dislike for getting up at five in the morning. It is the worst thing for you.
Your friend does not just dislike spinach, he feels very strong dislike for it. It is the opposite of loving.
Your brother cannot stand losing at cards. Which verb means 'to hate'?
b1-n-bericht: After the business trip your boss wants a written summary of what you did.
The news on TV includes a short film and text about the flood in the north.
A student writes about her internship and lists everything in a paper for her teacher.
b1-n-kraftwerk: Near the river there is a big building with tall chimneys that makes the electricity for the city.
Water falls through big machines in a dam to create electricity.
A storm cuts off the power, and the company says the place that produces electricity has a fault.
b1-adj-digital: Your old clock has hands, but the new one shows numbers on a screen.
The photos on your phone are stored as files, not as paper prints.
The company stops sending paper documents, and everything is now on computers.
b1-v-abmachen: You and your friend say 'let's meet at 5 pm at the station', and you both agree.
You peel the sticker off the bottle and take it away.
The boss and you settle on a price. Which verb means 'to agree on' something?
b1-n-laster: On the motorway a huge vehicle carries goods. It is much bigger than cars and loud.
A construction company brings sand to the building site in a heavy vehicle.
A driver delivers furniture over long distances in a big vehicle with a trailer.
b1-adv-angenehm: The room is not hot or cold, just nicely warm. Which adverb describes the warmth?
The music was quiet and nice to listen to.
You expected a bad hotel but it was better than you thought, and you were happily surprised in a nice way.
b1-n-buchhandlung: You want to buy a novel as a present and walk into a shop with shelves of books on the high street.
On Saturday you go to a shop to buy school books.
Which noun means a place where you buy books, not borrow them?
b1-n-saal: The wedding party takes place in a big room with many tables at the hotel.
The concert is held in a large room with rows of seats.
The school play is in a large room with a stage.
b1-v-vorhaben: A friend asks about your plans for the weekend. You say what you have in mind: a trip to the lake.
You are going to take a course next year. It is your intention.
Which verb means that you have something in mind to do?
b1-n-laerm: At 7 am construction machines work outside your window, and you cannot sleep.
In the classroom 30 children shout at the same time. It is very loud.
Your neighbors play loud music at midnight. Which noun means 'noise'?
b1-adj-zustaendig: Your internet does not work, and the hotline says another department is in charge of this problem.
At the town hall you ask which office is the right one for a new passport.
The boss asks who is responsible for the printer. Which adjective means 'responsible'?
b1-n-struktur: The teacher says your essay has no clear order: introduction, middle and end are missing.
Scientists study how the atoms in a crystal are arranged.
A company changes how its departments and managers are organized.
b1-v-sich-erkaelten: You went out in the rain without a jacket. The next morning you sneeze and have a runny nose.
Your child sat in the cold wind and now has a cough.
The doctor says: 'Dress warm so you don't get a cold.'
b1-n-metall: A spoon, a key and a coin are all made from this hard shiny material.
A magnet sticks to the fridge door because it is made of this.
Iron, copper and gold belong to this group of materials.
b1-n-schuld: You broke the vase, and your sister says: 'It is your fault.'
You owe the bank 5000 euros that you have not repaid yet.
You feel bad after lying to a friend. You have a heavy feeling of having done wrong.
